summary: David J. Kalupahana was a scholar of Buddhist studies and philosophy. He studied at the University of Ceylon and earned his PhD at the University of London under Stanley Weinstein and David Friedman, later holding posts at Ceylon and Hawaiʻi.

David John McCutchion worked in history, archaeology, and Indology after studying at Jesus College, Cambridge. He held teaching posts at Visva-Bharati University, Jadavpur University as Reader in Comparative Literature, and the University of Sussex as a visiting lecturer.

David Jones specializes in philosophy and religious studies and completed his Ph.D. at the University of Hawaiʻi at Mānoa. His posts include professor of philosophy at the University System of Georgia and director of the Center for the Development of Asian Studies.

David K. Wyatt was a historian who studied at Harvard, Boston University, and Cornell. He held posts at SOAS, the University of Michigan, and Cornell University, where he served as Chair of the Department of History from 1969 to 2002.

David Kerman Tomlinson specializes in philosophy and Buddhist studies. He studied under Jay L. Garfield and Andy Rotman, completed his PhD at the University of Chicago under Dan Arnold, and held a post at Smith College.

David Kopf worked in history, archaeology, and Indology. He studied at the University of Chicago from around 1960 to 1964 and held a faculty post at the University of Minnesota from circa 1967 to 1997.

David L. Gosling is a scholar of religious studies and Indology. He held a Spalding Fellowship at Clare Hall, University of Cambridge, in 1992, and was attested in a post at the University of Cambridge in 2001.

David L. Haberman is an Indology and religious studies scholar who studied at the University of Colorado Boulder. He held posts at the University of Arizona and Indiana University Bloomington, where he became Professor Emeritus of Religious Studies.

David L. McMahan specializes in Buddhist studies and religious studies. He taught at the University of California, Santa Barbara, and the University of Vermont, and held positions as Assistant Professor and Professor of Religious Studies at Franklin & Marshall College.

David Llewellyn Snellgrove was a scholar of Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He studied at Cambridge and under scholars including Giuseppe Tucci and Walter Simon, later serving as a professor at SOAS University of London from 1950 to 1982.

David Lopes was a scholar of history, archaeology, and Indology who studied at the Curso Superior de Letras and INALCO. He held teaching posts at Liceu Central, Curso Superior de Letras, and the University of Lisbon from 1902 to 1937.

David Ludden is a scholar of history, archaeology, and Indology who studied at Yale and the University of Pennsylvania. He held posts at the University of Virginia, the University of Pennsylvania (1981–2008), and New York University.

David M. DiValerio specializes in Tibetology, Buddhist studies, and religious studies. He studied at Wesleyan, SIT Graduate Institute, and the University of Virginia under Kurtis R. Schaeffer, before joining the faculty at the University of Wisconsin–Milwaukee in 2011.

David M. Knipe is a scholar of Indology and religious studies who studied under Mircea Eliade. He spent his career at the University of Wisconsin-Madison, serving as Professor of South Asian Studies, Chair of Religious Studies, and later Professor Emeritus.

David Matsumoto is a scholar of Buddhist studies. He served as Director at the Institute of Buddhist Studies and was attested as President Emeritus at the Numata Center for Buddhist Translation and Research in 2026.

David Max Moerman works in Japanology, Buddhist studies, and religious studies. He held posts at Barnard College and Columbia University, serving as Professor and Chair of the Department of Asian and Middle Eastern Cultures at Barnard College.

David Mitchell specializes in linguistics and Indology. He completed degrees at Cleveland State University and Ohio State University, and took up a post as Assistant Professor at Metropolitan State University of Denver in 2015.

David N. Lorenzen is a scholar of Indology, religious studies, and history. He studied at Wesleyan, SOAS, and the Australian National University under Arthur Llewellyn Basham, and served as Professor and Emeritus Professor at El Colegio de México.

David Oliver Allen was an Indology and history scholar who studied at Amherst College and Andover Theological Seminary. He served as a missionary with the American Board of Commissioners for Foreign Missions and as editorial superintendent at the American Mission Press.

David Ownby specializes in history, Sinology, and religious studies. After earning his Ph.D. at Harvard, he taught at Southern Methodist University and served as Professor of History at the Université de Montréal from 1994 to 2023.
